subject: geography
title: Representation of Places
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on place representation, statistics and qualitative sources.

concepts.def: Numerical: census, ONS data, IMD scores.
Decennial UK survey; 2021 census complete; cost £900 million.
Index of Multiple Deprivation; ranks small areas (LSOAs).
Active promotion via slogans, brands; 'I Love NY'.

walkthroughs.body_html: UK Census 2021: 56.5 million people in England and Wales; 84 percent urban. ONS data covers life expectancy gap: 9.5 years between richest and poorest London boroughs. IMD 2019 ranks Jaywick (Essex) as most deprived LSOA in England. Crime stats from police.uk.

Daniel Defoe's Tour Through Great Britain (1724-26) captured early modern places. Charles Booth's London poverty maps (1898). Modern: BBC documentaries, novels (Zadie Smith's NW), music (Arctic Monkeys' Sheffield). Each offers situated knowledge.

Manchester rebranded as 'Original Modern'; Northern Powerhouse since 2014. Marketing budget £6 million annually. Iconic projects: Etihad Stadium, MediaCity, Beetham Tower. Critics: marketing masks deprivation in Gorton and Cheetham Hill. Brand vs lived experience tension.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary data in geography fieldwork?
options: Primary data is more important and secondary data is less reliable.
Primary data is collected first-hand by the researcher (surveys, measurements, observations); secondary data already exists and is found in sources (census data, maps, published reports).
Primary data is collected in primary schools and secondary data in secondary schools.
Qualitative data means high-quality data and quantitative means a lot of data.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between qualitative and quantitative data?
options: Quantitative data is always more scientific and reliable than qualitative.
Quantitative data is numerical and measurable (traffic counts, river width); qualitative data is descriptive and non-numerical (interview quotes, photo descriptions, field sketches).
Qualitative data means high-quality data and quantitative means a lot of data.
Primary data is collected in primary schools and secondary data in secondary schools.

mcqs.q: Why are composite volcanoes more explosive than shield volcanoes?
options: Composite volcanoes have high-silica, viscous magma that traps gas, causing pressure to build until violent eruption; shield volcanoes have runny basaltic lava that releases gas easily.
Because composite volcanoes are found in cold climates.
Because composite volcanoes are taller and have more lava.
Qualitative data means high-quality data and quantitative means a lot of data.
